content:
Hi all, I’m preparing a PR adding two definitions for simple graph walks:

def Walk.IsChord (p : G.Walk u u) (v w : V) : Prop :=
  v ∈ p.support ∧ w ∈ p.support ∧ G.Adj v w ∧ s(v, w) ∉ p.edges

def Walk.IsChordless (p : G.Walk u u) : Prop :=
  p.IsCycle ∧
    ∀ ⦃v w : V⦄, v ∈ p.support → w ∈ p.support → G.Adj v w → s(v, w) ∈ p.edges

I’m unsure about file placement:
1) Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Paths.lean
2) a new file (e.g. ...)

Given current mathlib organization, where would you prefer these definitions to live?
If placement is agreed, I’ll open a draft PR with only these defs + minimal lemmas.

I haven't worked much on graph theory, so maybe wait until someone more experienced chimes in (cc @Kyle Miller), but I think it makes sense to create a new file Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Walks.Chords or similar.
(I'm surprised that Paths.lean is not in the Walks subfolder)

Alright, thank you for your reply and for the very reasonable suggestion. I’ll wait for input from more experienced contributors, since I’ve never submitted a PR to mathlib before and I want to avoid harming mathlib’s high-quality files and code structure.

I’ve submitted a draft PR on GitHub here: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/35906 . Comments, corrections, and suggestions are very welcome, and I’d be grateful if people could point out any issues.

FWIW: Mathlib usually prefers defs to come with a bunch of API, and it's recommended to split the PRs into (def + API) + (def + API) rather than (def + def) + (API + API).
Can you think of more useful theorems for chords? What is your motivation to add them, can you maybe include some of that motivation in the PR?

Thanks, that is helpful.

My motivation comes from graph-structural arguments about induced cycles / chordless cycles. In a proof I have already completed, I needed to choose a chordless cycle and then analyze bridges and attachment sets relative to that cycle. So the point of adding Walk.IsChord is to have a clean way to talk about an ambient edge between two vertices of a cycle that is not one of the cycle edges, and then Walk.IsChordless packages the induced-cycle condition.

I agree that the PR should contain more API. I have now expanded it so that each definition comes with some basic theorems:

  • for IsChord: symmetry and an isChord_iff theorem under the natural hypotheses;
  • for IsChordless: projection to IsCycle, a theorem that ambient edges between support vertices lie in p.edges, a not_isChord theorem, and an equivalence isChordless_iff_forall_not_isChord.

The current API is meant to be small but directly useful.

If people would prefer, I can also split this further into:

  1. IsChord + API
  2. IsChordless + API

That would be consistent with the usual mathlib PR structure.
